what_it_does: A Temporal Graph Neural Network (TGNN) learns from graphs — think of networks of people, transactions, or web links — where edges and nodes appear or change over time. Training these models is difficult because events must be processed in order: the model's internal memory for each node must be updated after every event involving it before the next event can be handled correctly. Processing events one by one is slow and leaves the GPU mostly idle, but grouping many events into a large batch to run in parallel causes the model to miss updates and degrade in accuracy. Cascade's key insight is to scan each batch for events that involve completely separate parts of the graph — nodes that never interact — and run those in parallel without breaking any ordering rules. For nodes that do share connections, the system checks whether two nodes' internal memories have become similar enough that processing them slightly out of strict order will not meaningfully change the result; when the memories are close enough, the strict dependency can be safely relaxed. A feedback loop also tracks which node memories change very little from update to update and skips redundant recalculations for those stable nodes.
